items.prompt: What is needed for any movement or action to happen?

options.why: Silence is not needed for movement.
Darkness has nothing to do with movement.

items.explanation: Energy is needed for anything to move or change.

items.prompt: Which of these is a form of energy we can feel or sense?

options.why: A shadow is an area where light is blocked.
A stone is an object, not a form of energy.

hints: Think about what a hot cup of tea gives out.
A shadow and a stone are not forms of energy.
You feel this when you stand near a fire.
items.explanation: Heat, light and sound are forms of energy.

items.prompt: Energy is present in sound, light and ___.
hints: Think about a fire or the Sun.
items.explanation: Energy is found in sound, light and heat.

items.prompt: Where does the energy for a toy car with a battery come from?

options.why: The wheels only turn. They do not store the energy.
The floor does not give the car its energy.

hints: The car stops when the battery is flat.
Wheels and floors do not store energy.
items.explanation: The battery stores energy that is transferred to movement.

items.prompt: Can energy be made or destroyed?

options.text: Yes, a fire makes new energy.
options.why: A fire changes stored energy into heat and light.

options.text: No, it can only be transferred.
Yes, it is used up when a bulb lights.
options.why: The energy goes to light and heat. It does not vanish.

hints: Think about the rule for all energy.
Energy moves from one place to another.
It changes form but the amount stays the same.
items.explanation: Energy cannot be made or destroyed. It is always transferred.

items.prompt: A person eats a banana and then runs. What is happening to the energy?

options.text: The banana makes new energy while the person runs.
options.why: Energy is not made.

options.text: Energy stored in the food is transferred to movement.
The energy in the banana disappears.
options.why: It is transferred, not lost.

hints: Energy moves from one place to another.
items.explanation: Food stores energy. The body transfers it to movement and heat.

items.prompt: Sort each example into the form of energy it gives out.
hints: Think of what you see, hear or feel.
items.explanation: Torches and candles give out light, drums and bells give out sound, and radiators give out heat.

items.prompt: A bulb changes electrical energy into light. Why does it also feel warm?

options.why: Energy cannot be made.

options.text: Some of the energy is transferred as heat.

options.why: Light on its own does not make a bulb warm.

hints: Not all the energy goes where we want it.
Think of the energy that spreads out.
items.explanation: Some energy is transferred as heat to the surroundings, so the bulb gets warm.

items.prompt: A ball is dropped and bounces lower each time. Where does some of the energy go?

options.text: It is destroyed by the floor.
options.why: Energy is never destroyed.

options.text: Some is transferred as sound and heat.
It goes back into the ball and makes it bigger.
options.why: The ball does not get bigger.

hints: Listen to what happens when the ball hits the floor.
The ball and floor get a tiny bit warmer.
items.explanation: Each bounce transfers some energy as sound and heat, so the ball bounces lower.

items.prompt: Which statements about energy are true?

options.why: A battery stores energy that was put in.

options.text: Energy is only found in moving things.
options.why: It is found in light, sound and heat too.

items.explanation: Energy is transferred and never destroyed. It is needed for any movement.

items.prompt: Energy cannot be made or ___.
hints: The rule is that energy is only transferred.
It is the opposite of made.
items.explanation: Energy cannot be made or destroyed.

items.prompt: In a kettle, electrical energy boils water. What is the useful energy transfer?

options.why: A kettle makes a little sound but that is not the job.

options.text: electrical energy to heat in the water

options.why: It happens the other way round.

hints: What does a kettle do to water?
The job is to make the water hot.
Sound is not what we want.
items.explanation: The kettle transfers electrical energy to heat in the water.

items.prompt: Why do we say some energy is wasted?

options.why: Energy is never destroyed.

options.text: It is transferred in ways that are not useful for the job.
It is stored in the bulb forever.
options.why: Wasted energy spreads out into the surroundings.

hints: It spreads out as heat or sound.
We cannot easily use it again.
items.explanation: Wasted energy still exists but it spreads out as heat or sound, so we cannot use it for the job.

items.prompt: A bicycle dynamo lights a lamp when the wheel turns. What is transferred to the lamp?

options.why: It happens the other way round.

options.text: Movement energy is transferred to electrical energy and then light.

options.why: Something must be transferred to light the lamp.

hints: Energy is transferred through a few steps.
items.explanation: The turning wheel transfers movement energy to electrical energy, which the lamp changes to light and heat.

items.prompt: Which energy transfer happens when you rub your hands together to warm them?

options.why: It is the other way round.
No light or sound is needed.

items.explanation: The movement of your hands is transferred to heat.

items.prompt: A torch battery has 10 units of energy. The bulb gives out 3 units as light and the rest as heat. How many units become heat?
hints: Take the light energy from the total.
items.explanation: 10 − 3 = 7. The other 7 units are transferred as heat.

items.prompt: A lamp is supplied with 50 units of energy. It gives out 10 units as light. How many units are wasted as heat?
hints: The total energy stays the same.
items.explanation: 50 − 10 = 40. The wasted energy is 40 units, mostly as heat.

items.prompt: Which statement about energy is correct?

options.text: Energy gets bigger each time it is transferred.
options.why: The total stays the same.

options.text: The total amount of energy stays the same when it is transferred.
Energy shrinks to nothing when a battery goes flat.
options.why: The energy has been transferred away from the battery.

hints: It only changes where it is.
items.explanation: The total amount of energy stays the same. It changes form and place.

items.prompt: A flat battery in a toy has no energy left. What is the best explanation?

options.why: Energy cannot be destroyed.

options.text: The stored energy was transferred to movement, sound and heat.
The battery made too much energy.
options.why: Batteries do not make energy.

hints: Where did the toy get its power?
The toy moved and made noise.
The battery is not destroying anything.
items.explanation: The battery energy was transferred to the toy and its surroundings, mostly as movement, sound and heat.

items.prompt: Two lamps give out the same amount of light. Lamp A gets much hotter than lamp B. Which lamp wastes more energy?

options.why: Lamp B wastes less because less becomes heat.
Lamp A wastes more as heat.

hints: Heat is wasted energy for a lamp.
Compare how much heat each gives out.
The same light is useful energy.
items.explanation: Lamp A transfers more energy as heat, which is not useful, so it wastes more.

items.prompt: Put the energy changes in order for a toy car that runs on a battery.
items: heat and sound in the surroundings
hints: Start with where the energy is stored.
The motor is connected by wires.
End with the energy that spreads out.
items.explanation: Stored energy becomes electrical energy, then movement, with some heat and sound at the end.

items.prompt: True or false: Food gives your body energy.
hints: What do you eat before a race?
items.explanation: The energy in food is released when your body digests it, and it lets you move and grow.

items.prompt: True or false: Energy is used up and disappears completely when a bulb is on.
items.explanation: Energy is not used up. It is transferred from the electricity to light and heat. Energy is never created or destroyed.

items.prompt: True or false: A moving car has kinetic energy.
items.explanation: Kinetic energy is movement energy, which any moving thing has.

items.prompt: True or false: Wasted energy simply vanishes from the world.
hints: Where does a warm engine give its heat?
items.explanation: Wasted energy spreads out as heat into the surroundings, where it is not useful. It does not disappear.
